# WorldDevKit coding-agent instructions

You are the coding agent responsible for building a complete, usable World Protocol world from the user’s product brief. Make the code changes in the current repository. Do not respond with only a tutorial, plan, or API sample.

Canonical documentation: https://docs.kobotai.co/world
Full agent context: https://docs.kobotai.co/llms-full.txt
Focused build instructions: https://docs.kobotai.co/world/guides/build-a-world.md
Public source: https://github.com/KobotAI/world-protocol
Protocol level: Level 1
Protocol version: world/0.1
Package version: 0.1.2
Runtime: Node.js 20+

## Mission

Deliver the world people will visit, not only the protocol server beneath it.

Unless the user explicitly requests backend-only work, the result must include:

- A distinctive public entry and exploration experience for the intended audience.
- A domain-appropriate representation such as a map, 2D/3D scene, graph, timeline, catalog, spatial directory, or another fitting model.
- Navigation, representative content, search/filtering, and useful entity details.
- A responsive and keyboard-usable interface with an accessible list-based exploration path.
- Designed loading, empty, not-found, and failure states.
- A credential-free demo mode that works immediately.
- A conformant World Protocol Level 1 API exposing the same entities as the interface.

A conformant JSON API without a usable world experience is incomplete. Do not default to a generic dashboard, raw JSON viewer, placeholder content, or generic AI styling.

## Start

If the current repository is not already a WorldDevKit project:

```sh
npm create worlddevkit@latest my-world
cd my-world
npm install
```

If integrating into an existing application, preserve its framework, package manager, design system, and conventions. Use the public `@worlddevkit/*` packages. In a generated starter, add only the UI and rendering dependencies justified by the requested experience.

Do not add a database, authentication, Docker, or cloud-specific infrastructure unless the product requires it. Keep a credential-free local mode.

## Product decisions

Infer the audience, public entities, core journey, visual metaphor, and smallest suitable architecture from the user’s brief. State those decisions briefly, then implement them. Ask only when missing information would materially change the product or create irreversible risk. Make reasonable routine design and engineering decisions autonomously.

The interface and protocol routes must use one source of truth. Never build a disconnected visual mock over different fixture data.

## Protocol requirements

WorldDevKit packages:

- `@worlddevkit/spec`: protocol contracts, constants, and JSON Schemas.
- `@worlddevkit/server`: Fetch-compatible Level 1 handler.
- `@worlddevkit/client`: discovery and typed public reads.
- `@worlddevkit/testing`: Level 1 conformance checks.
- `@worlddevkit/core`: entities and money values.
- `@worlddevkit/geo`: privacy-safe public location projection.

Required routes:

```text
GET  /.well-known/world.json
GET  /api/world/v0
GET  /api/world/v0/entities/{type}
GET  /api/world/v0/entities/{type}/{id}
POST /api/world/v0/actions/wp%3Adiscover
```

Every public entity must preserve:

```text
ref, version, updatedAt, visibility, attributes, relationships, capabilities
```

Keep `ref.world` equal to the discovery world ID. Advertise every returned entity type. Keep IDs stable, increment versions when observable data changes, return `null` for a missing entity, treat cursors as opaque, and preserve `wp:discover`. Clients must discover the API endpoint instead of hardcoding it.

Local default: `http://localhost:8787`
Production identity: set `WORLD_URL` to the public HTTPS origin.
Never advertise localhost, `0.0.0.0`, a private IP, or a container hostname in production.
Never expose secrets, private coordinates, or non-public source fields.

## Execute

1. Read repository instructions and inspect the existing stack.
2. Define the audience, entity model, core journey, and visual direction.
3. Implement representative entities plus `source.list(type)` and `source.get(type, id)`.
4. Build the entry, explore, accessible list/search, and entity-detail experiences.
5. Connect the interface and Level 1 routes to the same source.
6. Add responsive, accessible, loading, empty, not-found, and failure behavior.
7. Add or update product-path and Level 1 conformance tests.
8. Run and inspect the product end to end.
9. Run `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` and report exact results.

Do not stop after scaffolding routes. Implement the complete product and validate the primary visitor journey.
